basis: Cor pulmonale with chronic restrictive respiratory impairment; kyphoscoliosis is the separately diagnosed skeletal cause, not skeletal damage produced by this heart disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: underlying kyphoscoliosis is a separate causal skeletal disorder; this concept denotes its cardiopulmonary consequence.

basis: Cortisol excess causes myopathy/bone loss in ~50-80% and skin atrophy/fragility in >50%. Hypertension (~70-85%) is separately diagnosed.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: common hypertension (~70-85%) is a separately diagnosed disease; direct cardiac or vascular damage is not established in ≥30%.

basis: Parasitic cyst infection; hepatic cysts occur in 80-99% and cholestatic disease in 30-79%. Pulmonary cysts occur in 5-29%, below threshold.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic cyst occupation occurs in 80-99%, with cholestatic disease in 30-79%; the infection is not defined as exclusively hepatic.

basis: Congenital cerebellar disorder; oculomotor dysfunction reflects neurologic disease. Strabismus 3/3 and ptosis 4/4 are selected small samples, insufficient to establish common intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: cerebellar eye-movement abnormalities are neurologic; sparse strabismus/ptosis reports do not establish intrinsic ocular damage in ≥30% overall.

basis: Developmental, skin and skeletal/joint abnormalities define syndrome; cardiac defects/cardiomyopathy have HPO frequencies of 30-99%. Frequent ocular and dental defects omitted by cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cardiac malformations/cardiomyopathy are common, with HPO frequencies of 30-99%; retained alongside the three defining phenotype axes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: joint laxity and skeletal growth abnormalities define the faciocutaneoskeletal phenotype; congenital myopathy is also a synonym.

basis: Joubert cerebellar malformation and intellectual disability; polydactyly in 6/9 (~67%) and rod-cone dystrophy in 3/8 (~38%). Hearing loss reported in only one assessed patient.

decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing loss in 1/1 assessed patient does not establish prevalence ≥30% across this subtype and is not a diagnostic criterion.

basis: Intellectual disability and seizures define syndrome; cataract/glaucoma in 3/6 (50%) and cleft palate in 2/6 (33%). Small hands/feet alone do not establish skeletal dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: small hands/feet and short stature are descriptive growth traits; substantive skeletal or joint dysfunction is not established as common.

basis: Mitochondrial disorder with demyelinating neuropathy; progressive distal muscle atrophy and functional loss are defining and affect most. Hearing-loss prevalence is unspecified.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent distal muscle atrophy represents actual tissue and functional loss, is defining/common (>30%), and belongs to this neuropathy's course.

basis: TCF3-PBX1 lymphoblast neoplasm affects blood/marrow; explicit lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma classification and B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma ancestry support the lymphoma mechanism rule.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: explicit B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma synonyms and B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma ancestry trigger the lymphoma rule, beyond lymphoid lineage alone.

basis: Congenital tracheal narrowing affects the airway. Cardiovascular malformations are frequent (30-79%) but are associated separate congenital defects, not damage caused by stenosis.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiovascular anomalies occur in 30-79%, but are separate associated congenital malformations rather than direct cardiovascular damage from tracheal stenosis.
